cause: AddFunction writes the pending std::multimap under m_queue_lock, while AddFunctionsFromQueue read empty() before acquiring that lock. The actual MSVC multimap empty() reads non-atomic _Mysize, which insertion changes. Concurrent session producer/consumer use therefore had a C++ data race even if the queue swap itself was locked.
live_path: WorldSocket::HandleConnectToFailed queues WorldSession::RetryInstanceConnection from the socket network thread through WorldSession::AddDelayedEvent. WorldSession::Update pumps that same FunctionProcessor on its consumer thread. This is an actual cross-thread use, not a hypothetical extra thread added to a single-thread queue.
repair: Acquire the existing recursive pending-queue mutex before even checking empty(). Keep the empty path free of a temporary-map allocation. Swap the batch while locked, explicitly unlock before active-map insertion/callback work. Existing clock, cancellation boundary, batching, stable equal-deadline order, public header/layout/API and single-consumer active-map contract retained. No added progression or connection success.
scope: Full current FunctionProcessor.cpp reverses exactly to pinned b08be202a by replacing only AddFunctionsFromQueue lock scope. Header unchanged. SizeQueue has no production callers and remains a consumer/idle observer; this change does not claim to make active-map APIs or concurrent KillAllFunctions thread-safe.
